ask: The hermes m010 finding claims that for traces with strong temporal locality, the Mattson stack-distance CDF at depth K approximates the LRU-K hit rate for C=K within error bounded by (1 - 1/K), because the backward K-distance b_t(p,K) converges to the stack distance Δ as K grows for highly-local traces. This bound is asserted but unsourced — no paper citation, no proof sketch, no empirical validation. Investigate: (1) has any published work proven or disproved this specific (1-1/K) error bound between Mattson CDF(K) and actual LRU-K hit rate at C=K? (2) what is the actual convergence rate of the backward K-distance distribution to the stack-distance distribution as K increases, and does it depend on trace class (stencil, pointer-chasing, random, database)? (3) for which trace families does the Mattson CDF serve as a valid upper/lower bound on LRU-K, and where does it diverge? Search: Neil et al. 1993 SIGMOD LRU-K paper, Mattson 1970 IBM Systems Journal, subsequent empirical comparisons of stack-distance CDF vs LRU-K hit rates, any trace-driven studies benchmarking the approximation gap. Return: paper citations with bounds, trace classes where the bound holds/fails, and whether the STEALABLE upper-bound idea is safe to use or needs the correction term.
